items.headline: FDA approves first-ever treatment for limb-girdle muscular dystrophy
items.summary: The FDA approved Welgemda, the first treatment ever approved for any form of limb-girdle muscular dystrophy, a rare inherited muscle disease that causes progressive weakness and breathing problems. In a trial of over one hundred patients, it improved walking speed and lung function compared with a placebo.
items.why_it_matters: Patients with this form of muscular dystrophy have never had an approved treatment option before now.

items.headline: FDA approves first new breast cancer hormone therapy in over twenty years
items.summary: The FDA approved Wilserdly, a once daily pill that blocks estrogen signaling, for women recovering from early stage, hormone driven breast cancer who are at risk of the cancer coming back. In a trial of more than four thousand patients, it cut the risk of recurrence or death by thirty percent compared with standard hormone therapy.
items.why_it_matters: It is the first new hormone therapy approved for early breast cancer in more than two decades, and it treats a subtype that makes up about seventy percent of breast cancer cases.

items.headline: Medicare's third round of drug price negotiations will save nine billion dollars
items.summary: The United States government said a third round of Medicare drug price negotiations will save nine point two billion dollars next year, a forty five percent reduction from what Medicare would otherwise have paid. This is the first round to include drugs given in doctors offices rather than only pharmacy drugs.
items.why_it_matters: It shows a federal program for lowering drug costs is continuing to produce real, growing savings for patients and taxpayers.
